title: Stop round-tripping state through map[string]any to compute the delta
description:
The core inefficiency. `mergePatcher.patch` (`go/merge.go:17`) unmarshals every push's full JSON into `map[string]interface{}` and deep-diffs it against the cached previous map. Caching `prev` already avoids the second unmarshal, but the new state is still fully decoded into boxed interfaces every single time — even when one leaf field changed.

## Sizes

Per push, at the profiled state size:

- input: **341,817 bytes** of JSON
- decoded into: **12,189 nodes** — 2,502 objects, 449 arrays, 5,790 strings, 2,814 numbers, 594 bools, 40 nulls, max depth 10
- cost of that decode: **1,585,544 B and 34,014 allocations, 8.4 ms** (~40 MB/s, ~4.6x payload in allocation)
- diff cost on top: +0.9 MB-equivalent, +928 allocs, +2.5 ms
- output: **median 215 bytes** (min 19 B; the 335,856 B max is only the initial snapshot)

So ~342 KB becomes ~34k Go objects roughly 3.7x/sec to produce a couple hundred bytes of patch. Process-wide that decode is **46.8% of CPU and 193.70 MB of the 460.95 MB allocated per 30 s**.

The distribution is what makes this fixable: `machines` is 277,156 of the 341,817 bytes, and between consecutive pushes essentially all of it is byte-identical — the churn is a handful of leaf fields (cpu/ram/disk/net percentages, token counters, a pid, a terminal `cols`).

## Approaches

1. **Raw-message tree.** Keep `prev` as a lazily-decoded tree of `json.RawMessage` per key. Decode a subtree only when its raw bytes differ from the previous raw bytes — unchanged subtrees collapse to a `bytes.Equal`. On the profile above that would skip decoding ~99% of the payload on a typical push.
2. **Token-stream diff.** Walk both documents with `encoding/json/jsontext` decoders in lockstep and emit the merge patch directly, never materialising `any`. Zero intermediate boxing, single pass.

Approach 1 is the smaller change and composes with the existing `objectDiff` for the subtrees that do change; approach 2 is the theoretical best. Prototype 1 first and measure against the task-1 benchmark.

## Correctness

Preserve RFC 7386 semantics exactly: deleted keys as `nil`, type change forces replace, whole-array replacement on any element change (`sliceEqual`). Keep the existing merge tests green; add nested add/delete/type-change cases.
